- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 73), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward 2–3 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 72+), model overestimates continuation → reduce forecast slope or add early reversal signal.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model often underestimates downside risk → add 1–2% buffer below forecast for 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment shifts → adjust for sentiment volatility: if sentiment swings >0.2 in 3–5 days, model should adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true turn.
- If true outcome is below 65 and forecast is above 68, model overestimates recovery → reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.
